title: Gates start from a clean PATH, with -I -S, and the repository root only while importing tools (A19, A31, A32)

context.task: Close A19, A31 and A32: the gates run outside the sandbox and today load an interpreter, site-packages code and repository-root modules that the agent can write. The design is docs/design/ARRANQUE_PUERTAS.md sections 2, 3, 5 and 7.

select.heading: 2. A31: la raíz del repositorio va delante de la biblioteca estándar
3. A32: el intérprete de las puertas se busca en un `PATH` con directorios del repositorio

problem: The gates (the six Python hooks, the git pre-commit with tools/git/commit_integrity.py, and the boundary-validator MCP server) run outside the Bash sandbox with the person's rights, and they trust three things the agent can write. A19: the interpreter's site-packages runs .pth files and sitecustomize at start-up, and -I does not stop it (site.py 3.11.6 lines 607-616); only -S does. A31: the gates do sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT) and then import standard modules not yet loaded (sqlite3, dataclasses, ast, subprocess, logging, pydantic), so a dataclasses.py written at the ungoverned repository root runs in every gate, also under -I -S; reproduced at hook level (docs/adversarial-audit/CASES.md, A31). A32: Claude Code finds python3, sh and git on its PATH, and an activated in-repository .venv/bin, writable by sandboxed Bash, puts the agent's own python3 first; neither -I nor -S helps; reproduced at hook level (CASES.md, A32). Appending the root at the end of sys.path is not a fix: the session interpreter (pyenv 3.11.6) has a top-level `tools` package in its site-packages (deepcode_hku) that would shadow the kit in the validator.
decisions: D1 The launcher is a POSIX sh file, tools/hooks/launch.sh, always invoked as `/bin/sh <its path> <script>`, so neither sh nor the launcher is looked up on the PATH and its mode does not matter. It uses no program outside the shell's builtins before the PATH is clean.

D2 <script> is a path relative to the kit directory, the physical parent of the launcher's directory (tools/): hooks/<name>.py, git/commit_integrity.py or boundary_validator/validator.py. The project root is the physical parent of the kit directory. Neither comes from the environment.

D3 PATH cleaning drops entries that are empty, relative, do not resolve to an existing directory, or whose physical path is the project root or inside it, keeping the order of the rest. Temporary directories are not dropped (pytest's tmp_path on Linux is under /tmp); that limit is declared in ARRANQUE_PUERTAS.md section 6.

D4 boundary_validator/validator.py runs with -I and without -S (it needs pydantic from site-packages); every other script runs with -I -S. The defence for the validator is where its environment is, not a check (ARRANQUE_PUERTAS.md 5.3).

D5 ACTUARII_PYTHON, when set and non-empty, is the validator's interpreter: it must be an absolute path to an executable file whose directory resolves physically outside the project root, and it is executed as given, not resolved, so a venv interpreter keeps its venv. Unset or empty: the first python3 of the clean PATH. Only the validator reads it.

D6 sys.path pattern for every gate that imports the kit (require_boundary_validation.py, require_contract_context.py, announce_governance.py, commit_integrity.py, validator.py) and for tools/install.py: insert the root at position 0 only if it is not already in sys.path, `import tools`, then remove the root again if this code inserted it. The kit's submodules then load through tools.__path__, and no other import ever searches the root. When the root was already there (pytest's conftest), nothing is removed.

D7 The validator's start-up checks run only when it runs as a program (__main__), before any module outside the standard library is imported; imported as a module by the tests it checks nothing and behaves as today. Entries inside the kit directory are exempt from the guard (tools/ is governed): run without -I, sys.path[0] is tools/boundary_validator.

D8 tools/git/pre-commit relies on git running hooks from the top of the working tree (githooks(5)) and execs `/bin/sh "$(pwd -P)/tools/hooks/launch.sh" git/commit_integrity.py`; it looks up neither git nor python3 itself.

D9 A launcher failure is one stderr line starting `[launch] ` and exit 2: for PreToolUse and ConfigChange hooks that is a denial, for the MCP server a server that does not start, for the pre-commit a refused commit. A validator refusal at start-up is one stderr line starting `[boundary-validator] ` and exit 2, with nothing on stdout.

D10 Hook decisions, their messages and the validator's responses do not change. deny_python_escapes.py, confine_review_reads.py, block_config_changes.py, session_python_gate.sh and the shim keep their code; only their commands change. INSTALL.md and the AGENTS.md section 9 declarations come in separate changes. A21 (non-object params in the validator) is not part of this contract.

D11 The new tests work on a copy of the kit in tmp_path (installed with tools/install.py as tests/unit/test_installer.py does, or copied from the working tree), never in the real repository: the live hooks of the session would load anything planted at its root or on its PATH. A venv for the tests is created in-process with venv.create(..., with_pip=False, system_site_packages=True), which sees pydantic; no `python -m`.

D12 Order of edits (AGENTS 6.5): launch.sh first; then the sys.path pattern in the hooks, commit_integrity.py and install.py (it works with the old and the new commands); then validator.py; then .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json and opencode.jsonc with their tests; then tools/git/pre-commit. The ConfigChange hook blocks the settings change from applying to the running session: expected, it applies to the next one.

D13 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; hooks-every-environment, tests/security/test_hooks_without_shim.py passes, the system-python environment included where /usr/bin/python3 exists; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: `/bin/sh tools/hooks/launch.sh <script>` refuses (D9) when <script> is missing, absolute, contains a `..` component, does not name a regular file inside the kit directory, or names a symbolic link; it runs nothing in that case.

Before looking up any program, the launcher replaces PATH by its clean form (D3) and exports it, so the interpreter and every process the script starts (git) resolve against the clean PATH. A PATH entry outside the root that is a symbolic link into the root is dropped.

For every script other than boundary_validator/validator.py the launcher execs the first python3 of the clean PATH as `python3 -I -S <physical path of the script>`; stdin, stdout, stderr and the exit status pass through unchanged. No python3 on the clean PATH: refusal (D9).

For boundary_validator/validator.py the launcher execs ACTUARII_PYTHON (D5) or, unset or empty, the first python3 of the clean PATH, as `<interpreter> -I <physical path of the script>`. An ACTUARII_PYTHON that is relative, not an executable file, or whose directory resolves inside the project root: refusal (D9).

Wiring, with hooks, matchers, groups and order unchanged: in .claude/settings.json each Python hook command is `/bin/sh "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/tools/hooks/launch.sh hooks/<name>.py` and the session gate is `/bin/sh "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/tools/hooks/session_python_gate.sh`; in .mcp.json the boundary-validator server is command `/bin/sh` with args ["tools/hooks/launch.sh", "boundary_validator/validator.py"]; in opencode.jsonc its command is ["/bin/sh", "tools/hooks/launch.sh", "boundary_validator/validator.py"].
tools/git/pre-commit is the D8 form; a commit in a repository with the kit and that hook installed runs commit_integrity.py through the launcher, and refuses or accepts exactly as today.

require_boundary_validation.py, require_contract_context.py, announce_governance.py, commit_integrity.py, validator.py and install.py follow the D6 pattern: a module at the repository root named like a standard-library module (dataclasses.py, sqlite3.py, logging.py) is never imported by them.

validator.py run as a program (D7): it refuses (D9) when any sys.path entry resolves to the repository root or inside it, outside the kit directory; it then imports logging and pydantic without the root on sys.path; it imports `tools` by the D6 pattern and refuses (D9) when tools.__file__ does not resolve inside <root>/tools (a `tools` imported earlier from elsewhere, for example by a .pth); with a foreign `tools` package merely present in site-packages it starts and uses the kit's.

For the same payload every hook gives the same exit status, stdout and stderr as before, with the shim first on the PATH, without it and under the system Python where one exists; the validator answers initialize, ping and validate_proposal as before.

tests.must_catch: a launcher that runs a script outside the kit directory, a symbolic link, an absolute or `..` path, or nothing named, or that fails open
tests.reason: tools/hooks/launch.sh does not exist at the base commit

tests.must_catch: a gate that executes a python3, git or sh found in a directory inside the project root (also through a symbolic link from outside), in the hook commands of settings.json run as the harness runs them, the .mcp.json server command, or the pre-commit during a real git commit, in a kit copy (D11)
tests.reason: today the commands look python3 and sh up on the PATH and the pre-commit looks up git and python3, so the fakes run

tests.must_catch: a hook command or the pre-commit that runs the sitecustomize.py or an import line of a .pth in the site-packages of the python3 it uses (a venv in tmp_path, outside the kit copy, first on the PATH)
tests.reason: today no hook command passes -S, so site processes the venv's site-packages

tests.must_catch: a hook, commit_integrity.py through the pre-commit, or the validator through its .mcp.json command, that imports dataclasses.py, sqlite3.py or logging.py written at the root of a kit copy, or decides differently because they are there
tests.reason: today the gates insert the root first in sys.path and then import those modules (reproduced in CASES.md, A31)

tests.must_catch: a validator that starts with a sys.path entry inside the root (a .pth of its venv pointing into the kit copy's root) or with a `tools` imported earlier from outside the kit, or that fails to start, or uses the foreign package, when a `tools` package is merely present in its site-packages
tests.reason: today the validator has no start-up checks, and the D6 pattern does not exist

tests.must_catch: an ACTUARII_PYTHON that is relative or whose directory is inside the root and is used anyway, or a valid one that is not the interpreter the server runs under
wiring that differs from B5 or a pre-commit that differs from D8, in .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, opencode.jsonc and tools/git/pre-commit
tests.reason: the existing wiring tests pin today's `python3 ...` and `sh ...` commands; updated to B5 they fail at the base

tests.must_catch: a hook whose decision changes with the new commands, with the shim, without it or under the system Python, or that fails from another working directory
tests.reason: the existing behaviour tests, reading the script name from the last argument of each command, pass at the base and must still pass

commit_message: fix(puertas): PATH limpio con /bin/sh, -I -S y raíz solo para importar tools (A19, A31, A32)
